fixed: translateFeature drops the last residue that NCBI /translation includes when a CDS ends in an incomplete but unambiguous codon (major). Coding features (cds mode) now follow NCBI CSeqTranslator::TranslateToProtein: the 1-2 trailing bases are padded with N, and the residue is kept unless it is X (GC->A and CT->L are kept; GA->GAN and 1-base tails are dropped). translate() and cds:false still ignore the tail. Checked against 18 real NCBI records (19 CDSs, now in features.json): 12 kept tails including a complement(<1..65) CDS, 7 dropped tails, tables 1/2/4/11/13, codon_start 1-3, and a join. In a sample of 1,643 CDSs from 1,400 NCBI records, every /translation follows the rule. All 4,300 E. coli CDSs still match.

proteinIsoelectricPoint silently clamps pI to [4.05, 12] (major). When the root lies in [4.05, 12], the result is still Biopython's own bisection, bit-identical to Biopython (<1e-9). Otherwise the interval is widened until it contains the root. Results: FLAG 3.971 (ExPASy 3.97), protamine P1 12.075 (ExPASy 12.08), and charge(pI) is ~0 for every protein. stats.json gained pIRoot for all 460 oracle proteins; 64 of them were clamped by Biopython. Needs your sign-off on a spec decision, explained in the summary.

searchProtein accepts U and O in the peptide, but they can never match (minor). U now matches the codon TGA and O the codon TAG, whatever the table translates them to (cited: Zinoni 1986; Srinivasan 2002; Hao 2002). Ambiguous codons such as TGR do not match. search.json gained 200 recodedProteinCases (226 U/O hits, 117 on the bottom strand, 11 across the origin).

translateFeature accepts zero-length segments beyond L on circular records (major). A circular segment now needs start < L or must be exactly {L, L}, so an empty circular record accepts only {0, 0}. This removes the made-up bases ({30,30} gave 'MKPG') and the infinite loop on L = 0, which was reproduced as a vitest run killed by timeout.
searchProtein accepts U and O in the peptide (duplicate of the earlier U/O finding). Fixed by the same change.

Protein functions upper-case before validating (minor). stats.ts and searchProtein now fold only ASCII a-z, so 'ß', 'ı', 'ſ' and 'ﬁ' throw RangeError. Error messages give the original character, as a whole code point, and its index ('ß' at index 2).

baseCounts breaks its documented key order when the input contains digits (minor). Documentation fix, code unchanged: a Record<string, number> (the spec'd return type) always enumerates integer-like keys first (ECMA-262 OrdinaryOwnPropertyKeys), so the reproduction's order A,C,G,T,'1' cannot be produced. The TSDoc now states the real order: digits, then A, C, G, T, then by code unit. A regression test pins it. This is the docs remedy the reviewer offered.

Same root cause as U/O, found while fixing it: '*' could never match in tables 27, 28 and 31, where context-dependent stop codons translate to an amino acid. searchProtein now matches per-table codon classes (translation, stop status, TGA/TAG identity), so '*' matches context stops: 124 oracle hits.

Same root cause as the message defect: translate, searchSequence and dnaMolecularWeight printed a lone surrogate for emoji and other characters beyond the Basic Multilingual Plane. All error messages now share one helper (characterAt).
summary:
All seven findings are fixed; none was rejected. I fixed two more defects with the same root causes. No sudo was needed; nothing was committed and no dependencies were installed.

Every reproduction was first added as a permanent test and seen to fail. The infinite loop was reproduced as a vitest run killed by timeout. The module's 253 tests now pass (217 before). My files have zero tsc errors; the remaining package tsc errors are in other agents' files (test/review-tmp/gel-*, src/primers/design.test.ts). The full core suite has 10 failures, all in src/primers/*, which the primers agent is fixing and which import nothing from seqtools. The E. coli live oracle and the performance tests ran and are unchanged.

**Decisions for you:**
- **pI (finding 2) departs from the literal spec line "equal to Biopython within 0.01".** It stays exactly equal to Biopython wherever Biopython's [4.05, 12] interval contains the true pI. Outside it, Biopython returns the interval's edge, which is not a pI; its own docstring wrongly assumes no protein falls outside. It now returns the true root of Biopython's own charge model, which equals Biopython IsoelectricPoint.pi() given a wide enough interval, so I read this as the spec's intent.
- **No clamping to pH 0-14 either.** 200 Arg gives 14.30 where ExPASy shows 14.00.
- **ExPASy differences are documented.** I checked 21 sequences on ExPASy Compute pI/Mw (2026-10-08). ExPASy uses the same pK values except a C-terminal pK of 3.55 for D and E, so it differs when the protein ends in D or E (E10: ExPASy 3.29, ours and Biopython's model 3.47). It also clamps to 0-14.
- **New searchProtein semantics.** U matches TGA, O matches TAG, and '*' also matches context-dependent stops in tables 27, 28 and 31.
- **One known difference from NCBI, documented in TSDoc.** A /transl_except other than TERM on an incomplete last codon whose padded translation is X is still appended; NCBI appends only TERM there.

**Request for a shared file:** seq/range.ts sliceRange loops forever when L === 0 and end > 0, and reads extra turns for ranges with start ≥ L. translateFeature now validates its segments, but other callers of featureSequence or sliceRange are still exposed. Suggest `if (L === 0) return ''` plus validation in range.ts.

**Files changed** (all under /home/srdgjuchdr/HHereditas):
- packages/core/src/seq/translate.ts, search.ts, stats.ts and their .test.ts files
- tools/oracle/seqtools_oracle.py
- packages/core/test/oracle/seqtools/features.json, stats.json, search.json: additions only. The pre-existing content re-serializes to the old checksums, and regeneration is byte-deterministic.
- New: packages/core/test/oracle/seqtools/ncbi/*.gb — 18 verbatim NCBI records (100 KB), with download provenance in the oracle docstring.

seq/index.ts is unchanged: no new public API.
